sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source represents a system of blind faults confined at the footwall of the Acquasanta thrust activated during the 2009 Lâ€™Aquila and 2016-17 central Italy seismic sequences (Bigi et al., 2013; Tondi et al., 2020; Buttinelli et al., 2021).
This SW-dipping normal fault system was formed during the Mesozoic and reactivated during the Miocene flexure of the foreland in response to the orogenic build-up (e.g., Tondi et al., 2020). Some of the faults formed in the previous tectonic regime were transported onto the Acquasanta thrust hanging-wall (i.e., the Monti della Laga â€“ Gorzano fault, MLG), whereas their roots remained confined at the thrust footwall.
The interpretation of seismic reflection profiles in the area (Di Bucci et al., 2021; www.retrace3d.it) allowed to image the geometry of the Acquasanta thrust (Buttinelli et al., 2021), dipping toward W-NW. This evidence has shown that the southern segment of the MLG in the Campotosto Lake area is detached at shallow levels, thus indicating that the seismicity recorded in this area (9 April 2009, Mw 5.4, and 18 January 2017, Mw 5.7) has occurred below the Acquasanta thrust (Bigi et al., 2013; Buttinelli et al., 2021).
Historical and instrumental catalogues (ISIDe Working Group, 2007; Guidoboni et al., 2019; Rovida et al., 2021) show a very dense intermediate (4.5 < Mw < 5.0) to damaging seismicity within the region, like the 28 April 1646 (Mw 5.9) Monti della Laga, the 8 June 1672 (Mw 5.3) Monti della Laga, and the 7 July 1619 (Mw 5.3) Aquilano earthquakes.

pictures.t: Map of the 2009 seismic sequence and active faults
pictures.c: Map and cross-sections showing the 2009 earthquake seismic sequence and the Quaternary surface faults (from EMERGEO Working Group [2009]).

pictures.t: Geological data in Mt. Gorzano area
pictures.c: Geological and seismological data. The projection of the 2009 earthquake sequence onto the geological cross-sections shows that the 2009 sequence developed in a deeper thrust sheet on a fault plane independent from the Gorzano fault (Bigi et al., [2013])

pictures.t: Subsurface map of the Marne a Fucoidi formation (Buttinelli et al., 2021)
pictures.c: Subsurface map of the Marne a Fucoidi formation below the Monti della Laga area. Gray dashed lines in panel b represent the normal fault recognized below the Acquasanta thrust. Blue solid lines represent normal faults recognized in the hangingwall of the Acquasanta thrust. From Buttinelli et al., 2021

pictures.t: Central Apennines seismicity after 2016-17 seismic sequence
pictures.c: Relocated events of the 2016-17 seismic sequence in Central Apennines (Michele et al., [2020])

pictures.t: Map and cross-sections of relocated earthquakes of the 2009 sequence
pictures.c: Relocated events of the 2009 earthquake sequence, the cross-sections show the geometry at depth of the seismogenic source (pannel b) and its position respect to nearby sources (panel c) (from Chiarabba et al. [2009]). Note the cutoff of the seismicity at 2-3 km of depth (Sez-2, panel b) and its projection towards the Paganica Fault surface trace.

pictures.t: Map of the relocated 2009 earthquake sequence
pictures.c: Map of relocated events of the 2009 earthquake sequence and traces of Quaternary normal faults (from Chiarabba et al. [2009]). The Mw 5.4, 9 April 2009 aftershock and the related sequence activated a structure located to the NNE, with a right en-echelon step respect to the Mw 6.3 earthquake seismogenic source.

pictures.t: Deformation pattern induced by the January 2017 earthquakes
pictures.c: Deformation fields induced by the 18 January 2017 events. Interferograms by the Sentinel-1 mission  (Falcucci et al., [2018])

pictures.t: Ground deformation induced by the 18 January 2017 earthquakes
pictures.c: Modeled and observed DInSAR data (panels a, c, and d), GPS data (panel e), and fault dislocation model (panel b) of the 18 January 2017 events. Highest slip values are located in an about 5 Ã— 5 km2 region, spanning 3- to 9-km depth, with a peak slip of about 0.58 m (Falcucci et al., [2018])
